title: Adaptive multiplexed query broker for multi-tenant dashboard pagination
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Some of our dashboard queries that back the tenant usage views exhibit high p99 tail latency when multiple long-scroll pagination requests are executed concurrently by different tenants. Root causes include hot shard contention on time-windowed indexes, small-window cache eviction chatter, and per-request planning overhead for large result sets.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive 'multiplexed query broker' in the console backend that will: 1) detect similar pagination/scrolling queries across tenants (same route + overlapping time windows), 2) multiplex them into a single work unit at the planner level, 3) shard and serve results incrementally with shared, eviction-aware in-memory slices, and 4) provide hedged reads for long-tail pages. The broker will maintain lightweight fingerprints for in-flight windows and coordinate result fanout to multiple requestors while keeping tenant-level rate limits and isolation guarantees.

Design details:
- Query fingerprinting: hash(route + canonicalized filters + time-bucket) to group compatible requests.
- Multiplex strategy: if fingerprint group size > 1 and estimated total rows > threshold, run a single scan/aggregate and stream partial pages to each client.
- Shared window cache: replace per-request LRU with a hot-window cache keyed by fingerprint+page-token with TTL and access-weight eviction.
- Hedging: for requests exceeding configured latency (configurable per-tenant SLO), issue a secondary read from a cold replica or smaller index to reduce p99.
- Backpressure & fairness: the broker enforces per-tenant concurrency tokens and enforces max-fanout to avoid amplification effects.
- Observability: instrument broker with metrics (group_size, multiplex_rate, cache_hit_ratio, avg_fanout, hedged_reads, p50/p95/p99 latencies) and tracing linking requests to group run id.

Success metrics:
- Reduce dashboard p99 for paginated list endpoints by >= 35% under realistic multi-tenant concurrency tests.
- Increase effective cache hit ratio for long-window read patterns by >= 20%.
- No increase in error rate and maintain per-tenant rate limit isolation.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Complexity: introduces coordination layer and more code paths in the backend. Mitigate with small-scope rollout and feature flagging.
- Consistency: multiplexed runs must honor tenant visibility rules; careful canonicalization required.
- Resource usage: shared runs may increase peak memory usage for large fanout; include limits and memory guards.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in a feature branch behind the "mux-broker" feature flag.
2) Canary to 5% of traffic for internal/developer tenants for 1 week. Monitor latencies and memory.
3) Expand to 25% and run synthetic multi-tenant stress tests.
4) Full launch with toggle and emergency kill-switch.

Backward compatibility: The broker is transparent to API surface and only activates when compatible fingerprints are detected. Existing pagination tokens remain valid, but token issuance will be migrated to broker-managed tokens during rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runs end-to-end with fingerprint grouping and shared cache in staging
Synthetic multi-tenant workload shows >=35% p99 improvement for paginated endpoints compared to baseline
Metrics emitted for multiplex_rate, cache_hit_ratio, hedged_reads, and per-tenant fairness exposed in Grafana
Feature flag fully controls activation; emergency kill reverts behavior without token invalidation
Unit and integration tests cover fingerprint collisions, tenant isolation, and hedged-read fallback
notes: Related experiments in ENG-73421 and ENG-80012 showed benefits from group-aware prefetching; this ticket generalizes that concept to an execution-time broker. Coordinate with infra to ensure we have headroom for peak memory usage (see dependency ENG-44111).
